text:
“Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.”

- Oscar Wilde

Oscar Wilde (1854–1900) was an Irish poet, playwright, and novelist who became one of the most recognizable literary figures of the Victorian era. Famous for his sharp wit and observations about society, Wilde frequently challenged conformity, hypocrisy, and the expectations people place upon one another.

“Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.”

The line sounds simple, but the idea behind it carries a deeper meaning: in trying too hard to become someone else, you risk losing the person you already are. Society constantly offers examples of how we are supposed to look, behave, think, succeed, and live.

Following someone else’s path can feel easier because the route has already been established. But no other person shares your exact combination of experiences, circumstances, strengths, and perspective. Trying to recreate another person’s identity can mean trading something genuinely your own for something borrowed.

The humor of the quote also points to the futility of comparison. Everyone else’s identity is already occupied, so becoming another version of them contributes little. Authenticity isn’t about being different simply to stand apart—it’s about refusing to abandon your own identity in pursuit of someone else’s.

The larger message is simple: the world already has everyone else. Your challenge is to understand who you are, develop that person fully, and have the courage to remain yourself.

text:
10 Conspiracy Theories That Are Actually True

For decades there have been people in our societies who we’ve ridiculed and labeled paranoid due to their belief that the government is involved in various secret conspiracies. More often than not, these individuals or groups are depicted as crazy and the general public will often sneer at those who believe the government is made up of lizard people or that they’ve been abducted by aliens.
Although those two examples are a little unbelievable, what if the other conspiracy theories were real? What if the government really did hide things from the public and conduct experiments on their people? What if they planned terrorist attacks to start otherwise illegal wars? Time to put your tinfoil hats on because every single one of these ten conspiracy theories was proven to be true:
1. Project MK ULTRA
Conspiracy Theory: The CIA conducted experiments on US citizens.
Using drugs, hypnosis, sensory deprivation and even sexual abuse, the CIA tortured numerous US citizens in an attempt to develop a Truth Serum that could be used on communist spies. These experiments apparently took place throughout the USA in over 80 institutions, including hospitals, prisons and universities.
Ken Kesey, author of One Flew Over The Cuckoo’s Nest, has stated that he became involved in MK ULTRA whilst he was a student at Standford University. Having never done drugs before, Kesey was given LSD and other psychedelic drugs as part of the experiment.
“[The testing] wasn’t being done to try to cure insane people, which is what we thought,” Kesey told reporters. “It was being done to try to make people insane—to weaken people, and to be able to put them under the control of interrogators.”
Infamous gangster Whitey Bulger, lyricist Robert Hunter, singer Ruth Kelley and various TSS agents were also experimented upon. It’s thought that at least one victim, biochemist Frank Olson, died due to the experiments.
Project MK ULTRA began in the 1950s and ended in the 1970s after the Freedom of Information Act revealed 20,000 classified documents. However, CIA Director Richard Helms destroyed the worst MK ULTRA files in 1973 so a lot of the information was lost. The conspiracy theory was seemingly confirmed when President Bill Clinton issued a formal apology on behalf of the US government in 1995, however some suggest that this apology was actually about human radiation testing.
2. The Gulf of Tonkin Incident
Conspiracy Theory: The Gulf of Tonkin Incident, which caused the US to become involved in the Vietnam War, never actually happened.
Otherwise known as the USS Maddox Incident(s), The Gulf of Tonkin Incident occurred when two American destroyers apparently engaged with three North Vietnamese Navy torpedo boats that successfully managed to sink one of the destroyers.
President Lyndon B. Johnson then drafted the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, the legal justification for the USA’s involvement in Vietnam. However, the Gulf of Tonkin Incident never occurred.
A declassified National Security Agency study was published in 2005 stating that there were absolutely no North Vietnamese ships present at the incident. In 1965, even President Johnson himself said: “For all I know, our Navy was shooting at whales out there.”
3. The Tuskegee Syphilis Experiment
Conspiracy Theory: The US Public Health Service failed to treat African American men who had syphilis.
Between 1932 and 1972, the US Public Health Serviceconducted a clinical study on 400 African American men who were suffering with syphilis. The PHS failed to tell the men they had an STD and did not offer any form of treatment. Instead, many of the patients were told they had ‘bad blood’.
At the beginning of World War II, 250 of the men who had been studied registered to go to war, and only then were they told they had an STD. They were still denied treatment.
By the 1970s, 128 of the men had died due to syphilis, whilst 40 of their wives had the disease and 19 children had been born with congenital syphilis.
4. CIA Drug Trafficking in LA
Conspiracy Theory: The CIA enabled the sale of cocaine to street gangs in Los Angeles, then took million of dollars in drug profits to a Latin American guerilla army.
According to Pulitzer Prize winning journalist Gary Webb’s 20,000 word article Dark Alliance: The CIA, the Contras, and the Crack Cocaine Explosion, the CIA helped to deliver cocaine into the US so that it could be given to street gangs like the Crips and Bloods. They then took the profits and gave it to Nicaraguan Contras.
“This drug network,” Webb stated in the article, published in 1996 in San Jose Mercury News “opened the first pipeline between Colombia’s cocaine cartels and the black neighborhoods of Los Angeles, a city now known as the ‘crack’ capital of the world. The cocaine that flooded in helped spark a crack explosion in urban America . . . and provided the cash and connections needed for L.A.’s gangs to buy automatic weapons.”
Webb was later found dead on December 10, 2004 having apparently committing suicide. We say ‘apparently’ because he used two bullets to shoot himself in the head.
5. Operation Northwoods
📷Conspiracy Theory: The Joint Chiefs of Staff in the US military drafted and approved acts of terrorism in the USA so the public would support a war with Cuba.
Throughout the early 1960s, American military officials concocted multiple acts of deception, aiming to sway the USA civilians to support a war to oust Fidel Castro from power in Cuba. The plans, which are available to read here, included acts of terrorism in Washington D.C and Miami, killing innocent civilians and soldiers, bombing U.S. naval vessels, assassinating Cuban émigrés, sinking Cuban refugee boats and hijacking planes. The documents also state that they planned to fabricate evidence implicating Fidel Castro and Cuban refugees.
Fortunately, President Kennedy rejected the plan and they were kept secret for forty years.
6. Operation Mockingbird
Conspiracy Theory: The CIA paid journalists to publish propaganda.
Towards the end of the 1940s, when the Cold War was just beginning, the CIA began to pay major media publications and journalists so that they would share CIA propaganda.
Frank Wisner, Allen Dulles, Richard Helms and Philip Graham of The Washington Post worked together to found Operation Mockingbird, and eventually managed to enlist journalists from ABS, NBC, CBS, Time, Newsweek, Associated Press, United Press International, Reuters, Hearst Newspapers, Scripps-Howard, Copley News Service and many more. The Church Committee finally exposed the operation in 1975, though many believe similar activities are occurring to this day.
7. Operation Snow White
Conspiracy Theory: The Church of Scientology infiltrated the US government and stole sensitive information.
Although every other verified conspiracy serves to prove the US government is a force to be reckoned with, it was infiltrated by the Church of Scientology throughout the 1970s. It wasn’t until 1977 that the FBI was able to prove that over 5,000 Scientology members had been stealing classified information from 136 agencies, organisations and foreign embassies.
Scientologist leaders said that the operation was meant to expose “all false and secret files of the nations of operating areas” and to enable Church seniors and L. Ron Hubbard himself to “frequent all Western nations without threat.”
8. COINTELPRO
📷Conspiracy Theory: The FBI deliberately discredited and smeared political activists.
COINTELPRO, which stands for Counter Intelligence Program, was a series of covert, illegal operations conducted by the FBI during the 1960s that aimed to disrupt and discredit activists in the USA. Between 1956 and 1971, 85% of COINTELPRO resources were used to infiltrate, disrupt, marginalize and subvert groups that threatened the existing social and political order. These groups included those involved in the women’s rights movement, militant Black Nationalist groups and non-violent civil rights movements such as those inspired by Martin Luther King Jr. The other 15% was used to marginalize white hate groups like the Ku Klux Klan and the National States’ Rights Party.
9. The US Government Spies On US Citizens
Conspiracy Theory: The US government taps into the population’s phones and hacks into their computers to collect data on them.
For years conspiracy theorists that believed the US government was spying on their every move were told they were paranoid and crazy. However, when the NSA and their Prism Project was revealed to be illegally listening into our phonecalls and collecting data for over a decade, the general public began to wise up.
The government was adamant that the data was being collected as a matter of national security, but it’s becoming increasingly clear that the NSA hasn’t protected the American population from terrorists and may even be making life for them unsafe.
In June 2014, The Washington Post claimed that almost 90% of data that the NSA collected was from Internet users with absolutely no connection to terrorist activities, which is a clear violation of the constitution.
10. Governments Around The World Decide The Global Economic Policy In Secret
Conspiracy Theory: The world is governed by corporations.
In 2013, Wikileaks released secret documents that exposed the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) Intellectual Property Rights Chapter. The documents revealed a closed-door regional free trade agreement was being negotiated by Australia, Brunei Darussalam, Canada, Chile, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Peru, Singapore, Vietnam and the USA.
The Electronic Frontier Foundation responded to this revelation stating that the TPP has “extensive negative ramifications for users’ freedom of speech, right to privacy and due process, and [will] hinder peoples’ abilities to innovate.”
Later, in June 2014, WikiLeaks also revealed the Trade in Services Agreement (TiSA), which included fifty countries around the world that had agreed to promote privatization. The agreement prevented governments from placing public services back into the public hands and made it significantly harder to enforce environmental regulations.

text:
Tomorrow, we’re publishing a new article about Captain John Smith, co-written with my good friend Will Tanner.

Here’s a little teaser of what’s to come…

It was in these bloody campaigns that Smith rose to fame. Serving alongside Count Meldritch at the Siege of Regall, Smith and the Christian army found themselves locked in a demoralizing stalemate with the Turks, who were holed up in a heavily fortified stronghold. During the monotony of the siege, the Turkish commander–a fellow named Turbashaw–sent out an offer of single combat. He would fight any Christian champion in full view of both armies. Smith, eager for glory, accepted the challenge. As both sides watched, the two champions rode out onto the field, then raced towards each other, lances levelled. Smith’s lance smashed into the Turk, crashing against his armor and unhorsing him. Wheeling about, Smith raced back to unhorsed Turbashaw, hopped off his own horse, and used his falchion to cleanly decapitate the Turk. The army of Christ roared with applause at the gory trophy as the Muhammedans sat outraged.

It didn’t end there. Infuriated by Smith humiliating Muhammed’s army with such a display, a second Turk challenged him to single combat, again in full view of both armies: give back Turbashaw’s head, or lose your own, a warrior named Grualgo roared. Smith accepted, and it was back to battle. Again lances shivered, but this time Grualgo–though wounded in the arm–remained atop his horse. The champions wheeled about and raced at each other again, firing their pistols at point blank range. Smith was smacked in the breastplate, but it held firm. Grualgo was seriously wounded, and toppled from his steed. Smith once again brought his falchion to bear upon the wounded Turk; a second head was taken.

.
The Roman legion of Christians, called the Theban Legion, under the presidency of their General, Maurice, numbered more than six thousand men. They marched from the East into Gaul, which was in revolt. They were camped near the Lake of Geneva, when they received orders to join with the others in a solemn sacrifice to the gods. They retired a little farther away, to a site today called Saint Maurice d'Augaune, in order to abstain, but were told to return and join in the festival with the others. They found themselves in the sad necessity of disobeying the command. It was not an act of felony for these brave soldiers, who had already fought many battles, but of heroic loyalty. Nonetheless, the barbaric prince gave the order to decimate the Legion. It would seem the emperor's messengers might have feared a forced resistance, but the disciples of Jesus Christ hoped for nothing but a peaceful victory over the world and the demon, with all his false gods.
.
The names of the soldiers were written on papers and placed in the caps of the centurions, for 600 were destined to perish as examples. These embraced their comrades, who encouraged them and even envied their fate. The plain soon flowed with the blood of the martyrs. The survivors persisted in declaring themselves Christians, and the butchery began again; the blood of another 600 reddened the waters of the Rhone. The others all persevered in their faith, and Saint Maurice sent to the tyrant an admirable letter, saying: Emperor, we are your soldiers; we are ready to combat the enemies of the empire, but we are also Christians, and we owe fidelity to the true God. We are not rebels, but we prefer to die, innocent, rather than to live, guilty. The Emperor, seeing himself defeated, ordered them all to be massacred. As the massacre began, these generous soldiers deposed their weapons, offered their necks to the sword, and suffered themselves to be butchered in silence.
.
Eternal Father, I wish to honor Saint Maurice and the Theban Legion, and I give Thee thanks for all the graces Thou hast bestowed upon them. I ask Thee to please increase grace in  my soul through the merits of this saint, and I commit the end of my life to them by this special prayer, so that by virtue of Thy goodness and promise, Saint Maurice and the Theban Legion might be my advocate and provide whatever is needed at that hour. Amen.

text:
Iran Says ‘Many Differences’ Remain With US After New Talks

@LibertarianInst 

A senior Iranian official said the two sides remain far from a potential deal after US and Iranian officials held their first known indirect talks since the ceasefire collapsed in July.

A senior Iranian official said on Wednesday that Tehran was reviewing Washington’s response to its peace proposals, but significant differences remain. The remarks followed indirect talks between Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

During his speech to the General Assembly, Trump said a deal with Iran was possible but also threatened to annihilate the Islamic Republic. “I have a big decision to make. Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world,” the President said on Tuesday. “Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?”

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian responded to Trump during his address to the UN General Assembly on Wednesday, condemning what he called ‘signs of a bullying mentality. He condemned what he called “signs of a bullying mentality.”

“We will never bow our head or bend at the knee,” Pezeshkian said, adding, “It must be understood by Mr. Trump and those who seek to bully us that we are ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations without accepting the language of force.”

A senior Iranian official told Kyodo News earlier this week that Tehran sent the US a new proposal that includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if Washington takes steps to lift its blockade and ease military pressure. The proposal was relayed to the US through intermediaries as top Iranian officials, including Pezeshkian, were preparing to travel to New York City for the General Assembly gathering.

Iranian state-affiliated media later disputed reports that Tehran had made such an offer.

The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz was a key provision in the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed in June. Under the MOU, Iran committed to allowing traffic through the waterway to return to prewar levels, but was given control over shipping in the Strait.

The MOU also required Washington to lift its blockade of Iranian ports. However, after the agreement broke down in July, Trump declared the MOU “over” and reimposed the blockade. Tehran has since argued that Washington must fulfill its commitments under the agreement before negotiations to end the conflict permanently can resume.

Since Trump declared the MOU dead in July, Iran has demanded that the US uphold its commitments to the agreement before talks for a permanent end to the conflict resume.

text:
She escaped Hitler when she was just two years old.

Nearly six decades later, at the age of fifty-nine and standing at the highest level of American government, Madeleine Albright discovered a truth her parents had kept from her for most of her life.

Prague, 1937.

A baby girl named Marie Jana Korbelová was born into a world that was about to change forever.

Before she reached her second birthday, Nazi Germany invaded Czechoslovakia.

Her family fled.

They first escaped to England, where they lived through the bombing.

Eventually, they made their way to America.

There, little Marie became Madeleine.

She grew up as an immigrant child in a new country, learning English, eating hot dogs, and building a new life in a place that seemed to offer her family a second chance.

But inside their home, there was one subject nobody talked about.

The past.

Her parents never told her about the relatives who had remained behind. They didn't talk about the family members who disappeared or the names that vanished from their family history.

Silence became their way of protecting her.

They wanted their daughter to have a childhood without the weight of everything they had endured.

So Madeleine grew up without knowing the full story of her own family.

She didn't know she was Jewish.

She didn't know that three of her grandparents had been murdered in concentration camps.

She didn't fully understand what her parents had survived or why they had chosen to keep it hidden.

For fifty-nine years, she lived without knowing.

In the meantime, she built an extraordinary life.

She earned a Ph.D. from Columbia University.

She raised three daughters.

She became one of America's leading foreign policy experts.

She spoke five languages fluently and built a career advising presidents and working at the highest levels of government.

Then, in 1997, everything changed.

Madeleine Albright had just been nominated to become U.S. Secretary of State, which would make her the highest-ranking woman ever to serve in the American government.

As part of the background investigation, *The Washington Post* began looking into her family's history.

What they uncovered stunned Albright.

Her grandmother, Růžena, had been murdered at Auschwitz.

Other relatives had been killed at Terezín and Treblinka.

Three grandparents.

All gone.

Madeleine was fifty-nine years old when she finally learned the truth.

After spending nearly six decades building her identity and career, she discovered that she was the daughter of Holocaust survivors who had never told her what had happened to their family.

Her parents had kept the secret because they loved her.

They wanted to give her a normal childhood.

They wanted to protect her from the trauma they carried themselves.

They wanted her to grow up American, hopeful and free from the horrors of the past.

But now she knew.

And she had to carry that knowledge into one of the most powerful diplomatic positions in the world.

Only weeks later, Madeleine Albright was sworn in as America's first female Secretary of State.

A former refugee.

The granddaughter of Holocaust victims.

Now one of the most powerful women in the world.

At fifty-nine, when many people might be thinking about slowing down, Albright was beginning one of the most important chapters of her life.

She helped expand NATO into former Soviet territory.

She confronted ethnic cleansing in Kosovo.

She pushed human rights into diplomatic discussions where they had often been treated as secondary to political power.

Her own history shaped the way she viewed the world.

"My mindset is Munich," she once said. "For most of my generation, it was Vietnam."

She had learned early that authoritarianism had to be confronted before it could grow into something much worse.

But Madeleine Albright also found a completely unexpected way to communicate power.

Jewelry.

text:
My two cents:
1. Understanding China is undeniably important, but taking on heightened risks of arbitrary detention makes little sense today.
2. Even if Washington could negotiate protections against outright detention, could it ever secure an exemption for students who speak their minds? Academic exchange requires reciprocity; without free expression, it devolves into one-way political indoctrination.
3. If the priority is learning and engaging with the Chinese-speaking world, free and open societies like Taiwan or Singapore offer far better, safer environments.

Sentimentality about past exchanges is natural, but as the idiom warns, carving a notch on the hull after the sword has fallen into the river is futile. Worse still, reaching into dark waters today is far more likely to yield a snakebite than a recovered blade.

text:
I’m usually not attacked for being naive on China. But I believe strongly in sending students, with appropriate protections, to China. I was one of these students.

I cannot see why our piece should be controversial, but realize there are some who believe all exchanges should be halted. I am not among them.

Here is our argument:

-Longstanding federal programs that encourage US students to learn about China — like Fulbright, CLS, and Boren — should be funded by the US government. We had similar exchanges with the Soviets, and of course with China, in the past.

- Given growing risks to students in China, those participating in these programs must be protected from harassment or threats of arbitrary detention, which are growing, and which are why these programs were difficult to renew in the past.

- But there is a way out. Summits provide an opportunity to achieve commitments that protect these programs and their students. Trump should (1) elevate these programs into leader-level deliverables, and (2) reach formal (or, more likely, informal) agreements to insulate them from politics. The former sends a signal not to touch these programs and the latter sustains it.

- As part of this effort, Min Zin and other scholars and students arbitrarily detained or exit banned by China must be released.

- We did not write this in the piece, but obviously these efforts should be accompanied by proper orientation and training for students before they visit China. That was also the case for these programs in the past. It is more criticism now.

We have done all this before. It has worked before too. Leader-level recognition of certain programs in China can provide protection.

The US desperately needs China expertise. After a surge among millennials, what expertise we did have faces a cliff as students lose interest in and opportunities for studying China and Chinese. 

That is a problem.

text:
SHANGHAI, SEOUL AND TAIPEI SIT OUT FRIDAY. TOKYO OPENS FIRST, WITH ITS BOND YIELDS AT A 30-YEAR HIGH:

US stock futures reopened at 6pm ET and have barely moved: Dow futures at 51,639.00, -78.00 / -0.15%; S&P 500 futures at 7,756.00, -11.00 / -0.14%; Nasdaq-100 futures at 30,723.00, -43.75 / -0.14%; Russell 2000 futures at 2,852.70, -4.10 / -0.14%, each since Thursday's close. The fund many investors use to own the index agrees: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) at $767.18, -$0.63 / -0.08% on Thursday, and $766.42 after hours, -$0.76 / -0.10% from that close.

The evening verdict: investors have not changed their minds since the 4pm bell, and tonight offers unusually few places to do it. Mainland China and Taiwan close Friday for the Mid-Autumn Festival, and South Korea is shut through Friday for Chuseok. The first major market to answer is Tokyo, which opens at 8pm ET - and Japan is caught in the same sell-off in long-term government bonds that set New York's close.

How Thursday finished: the S&P 500 at 7,704.13, -1.90 / -0.02%; the Dow Jones Industrial Average at 51,349.98, -161.61 / -0.31%; the Nasdaq-100 at 30,478.86, +8.56 / +0.03%; the Russell 2000 at 2,835.57, -3.09 / -0.11%. Flat on the surface. Underneath, borrowing costs kept climbing:
- 10-year Treasury yield - what Washington pays to borrow for ten years, and the base for mortgage rates: 5.18% on the Treasury Department's end-of-day reading, up from 5.11% Wednesday, the highest since 2007
- 30-year: 5.47%, the highest since 2004
- 2-year, which tracks bets on the Federal Reserve's next few moves: 4.87%, from 4.85%

Long-term rates are rising much faster than short-term ones. Lenders want more pay to tie their money up for years, whatever the Fed does next.

Oil added to it. US crude (November) settled - its official end-of-day price - at $94.61 a barrel, +$2.45 / +2.66%, and Brent, the global benchmark, at $106.60, +$3.52 / +3.41%, even after a midday Reuters report that US and Iranian negotiators are discussing a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Dearer oil feeds inflation, and bond buyers demand higher yields to cover it. US crude is at $94.27 tonight, -$0.34 / -0.36% since that settlement.

Tokyo gets the bond problem first. Japan's 10-year government bond yield rose 0.08 point on Thursday to 3.055%, its highest since 1996, in the first session after a three-day holiday. Stocks rose anyway: the Nikkei 225 at 65,513.94, +494.99 / +0.76% from last Friday's close, led by technology and AI shares. Nikkei 225 futures traded in Chicago stand at 65,530, -185 / -0.28% since their Thursday settlement. Why Tokyo matters here: Japanese investors are among the largest foreign owners of US government debt, and when their own bonds pay above 3%, the case for buying Treasuries abroad gets weaker.

China is the night's other story, and its main market cannot trade it. Xi Jinping's state visit ends Friday - tea at the White House, the National Archives, then the flight home. The deliverable so far came Wednesday, when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the trade truce would run to January 10 instead of November 10: two more months, not the "bigger deal" he said both sides are still weighing. Mainland investors got one session with that news. The Shanghai Composite closed Thursday at 3,888.37, -48.15 / -1.22%, a drop Business Standard tied to uncertainty over the truce. Shanghai and Shenzhen, and the Stock Connect trading links with Hong Kong, stay shut until Monday, trade three days, then close again October 1-7 for the National Day holiday.

That leaves Hong Kong, open Friday because its own holiday falls on Saturday, as the main market pricing any China headline from the summit's last day. The Hang Seng closed Thursday at 24,761.13, -72.99 / -0.29%, and reopens at 9:30pm ET.

The strongest fact against a quiet night: thin trading is not the same as calm. Oil trades straight through, and a statement on the record from Washington or Tehran about the Hormuz talks could move futures before any Asian market does. The VIX - the options market's gauge of how much the S&P 500 is expected to swing over the next month - closed at 15.67, +0.49 / +3.23%, well under its long-run average near 19.5. Investors are not braced for a surprise.

Friday and beyond, Eastern time:
- 8:30am Friday: the Census Bureau's advance report on August durable goods orders - orders for goods built to last three years or more, from aircraft to factory machines. July: $339.3B, +1.1%; +0.4% without transportation. Forecasters expect a dip of about 0.4%.
- 10:00am Friday: the University of Michigan's final September consumer survey. The early read on September 11: sentiment 47.8 vs 51.7 in August, the weakest since May's record low; households expecting 4.6% inflation over the next year, up from 4.0%, and 3.4% a year over the next five, up from 3.3%.
- Wednesday, September 30, 8:30am: August PCE inflation from the Bureau of Economic Analysis, the Fed's preferred price gauge, on quarter-end, when fund rebalancing can move prices with no news behind it.

The number that decides Friday is the 10-year yield against Thursday's 5.18%, and the report that speaks to it most directly is Michigan's year-ahead inflation figure. What would change tonight's flat read: that figure climbing past 4.6%, adding to the pressure that set Thursday's close, or falling back toward August's 4.0%, which would hand bonds their first real relief of the week.

Seoul, Taipei and Shanghai sit this night out. The market that opens first is Japan, where ten-year borrowing now costs more than at any time since 1996, and New York gets its own answer at 10am.

Not investment advice.

text:
Let's look at Tuesday's offer, shall we?

Basically: to reopen Hormuz in 7 days if Washington lifts the blockade on Iranian ports.

Well, while not many were looking a different deadline ran out yesterday (Wednesday).

The "D-Day" sanctions took effect on the 23rd: secondary sanctions on any company anywhere doing busines with Iranian airlines, aimed at grounding the civilian fleet worldwide.

Trump named it that, obviously.

So by midnight every Iranian flight to the UAE was cancelled, nothing Iranian on the Dubai of Abudhabi boards, Qeshm and Varesh grounded.

The countries still accepting flights are: Afghanistan, Armenia, China, Iraq, Pakistan, Tajikstan, Turkey.

Basically what happened was the day before Iran threatened to make any complying neighbour's airports "unusable".

The offer was ports for the strait. Looks like they might be including airports now...

Congresswoman AlmaS Adams

On Monday, I introduced the Faith-Based Affordable Housing Predevelopment Fund Act, a bill that would help expand the affordable housing supply by addressing a critical early-stage financing gap that prevents faith-based organizations (FBOs) from developing housing on land they already own.

Shelter is a basic human need, and housing is a fundamental human right. 

The average rent for an apartment in Charlotte is over $1,400 a month, a cost that is too high for many families. Faith-based organizations in my district and across the nation want to use their resources to build more affordable housing for their communities, but high upfront pre-development costs can be a major deterrent. 

The bill creates a five-year pilot program through the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to offer competitive grants to states, local governments, nonprofits, and community development financial institutions (CDFIs) to fund essential pre-development costs for FBO-led affordable housing projects.

text:
September 24, 1976

Cy Young Candidate Garland Set to Test Free Agent Market

On this date in 1976, “Baltimore’s chance of a miracle finish nearly evaporated even though the Orioles blanked the Boston Red Sox, 3-0, at the stadium for Wayne Garland’s 19th victory.”

“The shutout stretched the Orioles’ winning streak to five games and followed their shocking four-game sweep in New York. They now trail the Yankees by seven games.”

“The Birds, who are pulling one of their famous stretch runs for the third straight year, have won 18 of 26 during the month of September. They are 34-16 since August 5 and 46-26 since the All-Star Game break – the best in the American League.”

The win over Boston, “was a combination of Garland’s clutch pitching and a second-inning blitz against Boston’s Rick Wise, when the Birds scored all of their runs on four hits.”

“Garland struck out six and walked three in pitching his fourth shutout and boosting his record to 19-7.”

“’Way to go, Cy,’ someone said in the Oriole clubhouse….’Cy who?’ said Garland….”

Jim Palmer (22-13) and Garland “seem ready to duke it out for ‘Cy.’ Their prime competition is expected from Boston’s Luis Tiant (20-11)….New York’s Ed Figueroa (19-9), Minnesota’s Bill Campbell (16-5, 18 saves) and Detroit’s Mark Fidrych (16-9).”

“The Cy Young Award is based on a vote of two sports-writer’s from each team’s city, and who knows what influences those 24 persons around the American League – won-lost percentages, earned run averages, homeruns allowed, hairdos?”

“Garland rates within the top in all three categories. His won-lost log is second-best among the contenders, behind Campbell; his ERA is 2.60; he has allowed only 10 homeruns; and his hair is stylishly curly.”

When the Cy Young Award subject came up Garland simply responded, “’really, I can’t worry about things like that. It’s not up to me.”

“Garland is right” he has no control over voting, so he is concerning himself only with getting win No. 20, to him, ‘the greatest thing in my life.’”

Orioles’ manager Earl Weaver was asked “if he’d pick Garland or teammate Jim Palmer…for the American League’s Cy Young Award.”

“’You ain’t going to get me to comment on that,’ Weaver said, his diplomacy showing along with everything else as he toweled off after a postgame shower.”

Given his terrific season, what was clear was the fact that the still unsigned Garland was going to be one of the most sought after free agents during the offseason. “The 25 year-old, who reportedly would have agreed to a $250,000 offer had it been made early in the season, remains unsigned and now wants to test his worth on the open market as a free agent.”

“’I want to sign here, and I’d love to pitch here,’ Garland said. ‘I've told them that. But now, I’d like to see what I’m offered elsewhere, and then see if the Orioles will match it.’”

Gordon Beard – Associated Press
Ken Nigro/Michaeal Janofsky – Baltimore Sun

text:
St. Nicholas of Flüe
Confessor 
September 25th

[The following is a traditional reading for St. Nicholas of Flüe's feast translated from German.] 

“St. Nicholas of Flüe—born to respectable parents in Sachseln, Unterwalden (then part of the Diocese of Constance)—spent his childhood in singular innocence. In his youth, emulating Saints Nicholas of Myra and Nicholas of Tolentino, he imposed upon himself a regimen of fasting three days a week. He was so intent on divine contemplation, day and night, that he deeply yearned for a solitary life; yet, yielding to the insistence of his family, he entered into marriage, a union that produced five sons and as many daughters. During his time in military service, he is said to have miraculously saved the Convent of St. Catherine in the Canton of Thurgau from imminent pillage and burning through his intervention. Upon returning to his homeland, he steadfastly refused the highest magistracy—an office repeatedly offered to him—doing so most resolutely after a moment when, illuminated by supernatural light, he beheld sulfurous flames issuing from the mouths of corrupt judges.

As God continued to kindle in his heart a longing for a higher life, he abandoned everything and withdrew to a nearby wilderness, where he spent nearly twenty years living with extraordinary austerity. The miracles and virtues of this first hermit became so renowned that people from far and wide flocked to him, stirred by his reputation. During those years, he lived without earthly food or drink, nourished solely by the most holy Body of Christ. The authenticity of this miracle was confirmed by the Auxiliary Bishop of Constance. Through his unceasing zeal for virtue and constant contemplation of the Lord’s Passion, he provoked the fierce wrath of demons; yet he was also granted heavenly visions—most notably when the Most Holy Trinity appeared to him in the form of a radiant wheel, pouring into him such an abundance of divine rays and hidden wisdom that an extraordinary glow remained upon his face until his death. He instructed those who came to him—especially his fellow citizens—through many salutary exhortations, urging them above all to obey the Apostolic See and the clergy, and particularly to bring forth worthy fruits of penance—a message he himself proclaimed through his emaciated face and body, his rough habit, and his constantly bare feet and head. He was distinguished by the gift of prophecy and frequently discerned future events and hidden thoughts.

In Sarnen, the capital of Obwalden, he immediately extinguished a fierce fire by making the sign of the Cross. It is also worth recalling how, following a brilliant victory by eight Swiss cantons over the powerful Duke of Burgundy—when a serious dispute broke out among the allies that seemed resolvable only through combat—the blessed elder admonished them with a blend of firmness and gentleness, swiftly restoring them to harmony. For this reason, he is worthy of being called by posterity an architect of peace and a father of the fatherland. Finally, in the year 1487, while tormented by a severe illness and lying upon the bier that had served as his bed throughout his life as a hermit, he peacefully passed away on March 21st. His holy body—buried in the parish of Sachseln and distinguished by miracles—became an object of veneration for throngs of Swiss people and visitors from abroad. When Saint Charles Borromeo visited the site, he did not hesitate to call Niklaus a great saint. Pope Clement IX recognized and confirmed the veneration accorded to him by the faithful; ultimately, Pius XII enrolled Niklaus among the saints.”

(Officia Propria Diœcesis Curiensis, Reading for St. Nicholas of Flüe, Sept. 25th, Matutinum, Lectio IV)

text:
🚨 IT'S OFFICIAL: Trump Judges on the 6th Circuit REINSTATE Ohio's Proof-of-Citizenship Rule for BMV Voter Registration in JD Vance's Home State
By Jonathan Gregory 

OHIO - SEPTEMBER 24, 2026
In a 2-1 decision issued late Wednesday, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit stayed a lower-court injunction and allowed Ohio to enforce its 2025 law requiring documentary proof of U.S. citizenship before Bureau of Motor Vehicles clerks offer voter registration during driver's license or state ID transactions. The majority opinion came from Circuit Judges John Nalbandian and Whitney Hermandorfer, both appointed by President Donald Trump; they concluded the challengers had not shown eligible citizens were actually blocked from registering and that the district court's order arrived too close to Ohio's October 5 registration deadline. Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose immediately hailed the stay as a "huge legal victory for election integrity."

The ruling overturns, for now, an August preliminary injunction from Cleveland District Judge Solomon Oliver Jr., who had blocked the BMV-specific requirement on the theory that a signed citizenship attestation was enough under the National Voter Registration Act. The appeals-court majority found the plaintiffs, advocacy groups including Red Wine & Blue, likely lacked standing because they identified no would-be voters turned away solely by the citizenship-document rule; license denials in the record stemmed from other paperwork problems. Other registration channels in Ohio still rely on a signed attestation rather than documents. Supporters argue the measure simply aligns motor-voter offers with the citizenship proof already required to obtain an Ohio license in the first place.

Election integrity advocates say every state should adopt similar safeguards and that the U.S. Senate should pass a federal version so the same standard applies nationwide before November. Critics counter that noncitizen voting is rare and extra documentation can burden some eligible citizens; the stay is temporary pending the full appeal. With midterms weeks away and a competitive Ohio Senate race in play, the 6th Circuit's order means BMV registration in JD Vance's home state will again condition the offer of a voter form on proof of citizenship.

00:28 AI TESTED ON DUST LUNG X-RAYS
00:58 GRAB AIMS TO TRAIN 30,000 WORKERS
01:21 OREGON ORDERS AI SAFETY CRITERIA

TRANSCRIPT
A planned British AI supercomputer faces a grid connection delay that could stretch into the next decade. The Guardian reports that UK Power Networks told developer Nscale it could not supply enough power to the Loughton site until the early to mid-2030s, although the project had been expected to launch in 2027. Nscale says it is investigating on-site generation and faster connections, while the case shows how limited grid capacity can postpone promised AI computing and local benefits.

Researchers are testing AI as a second reader for the chest X-rays of workers exposed to dangerous dust. A Michigan State University team evaluated deep-learning models on 2,968 labeled images in a retrospective study published August 23, and says it is working toward packaging the technology as an application. With only about 200 certified readers for these X-rays in the United States, a validated tool could expand screening capacity, but this study does not show clinical deployment or improved worker health.

Grab and OpenAI have launched an AI training program aimed at 30,000 drivers, delivery riders and merchants. The two-year effort began in Singapore and is scheduled to expand across six Southeast Asian markets, with in-person lessons covering business ideas, sales, promotions and inventory. Participants are promised three months of ChatGPT Plus, but the 30,000 figure is a goal and the announcement offers no evidence of higher earnings.

Oregon has ordered a closer look at the safety of advanced AI used by state agencies. Governor Tina Kotek’s executive order tells the state technology chief to develop criteria for independent safety reviews and assess whether a kill switch for frontier models is viable. An implementation proposal is due within 90 days, while the final criteria remain unfinished and the order does not directly impose requirements on private developers.

A September 21 international appeal calls for independent checks before the most advanced AI models are released. Representatives of 20 governments and the European Commission asked companies to test models before deployment and urged governments to coordinate standards and share reports of serious incidents. The call is a political proposal rather than a binding rule, but adoption could change how powerful AI services used at work and in public services are reviewed.

text:
Secretary Kennedy asked for comment on how to revise the CDC vaccine schedule. Here is what we submitted on behalf of @ICANdecide on that score:

I. Every Vaccination Recommendation and Decision Should be Based on Shared Clinical Decision-Making (SCDM)

The central principle is straightforward: vaccines should be treated like every other medical intervention administered to an individual patient. The appropriate approach, therefore, is SCDM, where there is no “default” decision to vaccinate, but where “the decision about whether or not to vaccinate may be informed by the best available evidence of who may benefit from vaccination; the individual’s characteristics, values, and preferences; the health care provider’s clinical discretion; and the characteristics of the vaccine being considered” with no “prescribed set of considerations or decision points in the decision-making process.”[1]

This process should apply to every vaccine—period. HHS should therefore not treat SCDM as a special category reserved for a subset of vaccines or classes of vaccines; it is the appropriate clinical process for every vaccine decision. We urge HHS to adopt and implement this principle across the entire federal vaccine recommendation framework.

     A. Ethics and Informed Consent Demand SCDM

The RFI states that personal autonomy, informed consent, and the values and preferences of patients and parents “apply across all vaccine recommendations, including routine ones.” However, with the current categories, most of which are “default” decisions to vaccinate, that statement has no practical effect. A federal recommendation should not predetermine the medical decision of any particular patient.

This principle is consistent with ordinary clinical practice and ethics. The Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (“AHRQ”) describes SCDM as a collaborative process in which patients and clinicians make healthcare decisions informed by evidence, clinical expertise, and the patient’s values, goals, and circumstances.[2] The American Medical Association likewise recognizes informed consent as fundamental to medical ethics.[3] The fact that a vaccine is recommended by public health authorities does not eliminate the need for individualized clinical assessment or informed consent. Each patient’s medical history, risk factors, prior reactions, values, and preferences may affect the appropriate decision in ways a population-level recommendation cannot capture.[4]

The current federal framework classifies a majority of vaccine recommendations as a “default” decision to vaccinate. Other medical frameworks reject this approach: Clinical Practice Guidelines, for example, are designed to inform clinician-patient decision-making by presenting the evidence and the likely benefits and harms of available options, without dictating a one-size-fits-all course of care.[5]

There should not be any “routine” or “risk-based” recommendations. Population-level criteria cannot capture every clinically relevant characteristic of each patient, and applying them directly to individual decisions risks creating the false impression that harm-benefit tradeoffs are uniform across everyone who meets a given classification. In reality, individuals within the same risk group often differ substantially in their risk for the relevant outcome and in the balance of benefits and harms of treatment. Population-level classifications should never substitute for the individualized evaluation of all relevant patient attributes that determines whether an intervention offers a true net benefit to a specific patient.[6]

A clinician should never administer a vaccine based on a government recommendation but rather should only administer every vaccine based on SCDM which allows for informed consent and an evaluation of each individual’s medical history, competing risks, and personal values.

     B. Many Childhood Vaccines Do Not Prevent Infection or Transmission and/or Have Limited or Uncertain Community-level Impact

While all vaccines should be administered based on SCDM, without any exception, CDC’s existing guidelines already provide that most vaccines should be SCDM because they do not meaningfully prevent transmission. As CDC’s guidance provides: “ACIP makes shared clinical decision-making recommendations when individuals may benefit from vaccination, but broad vaccination of people in that group is unlikely to have population-level impacts.”

For example, DTaP, Tdap, IPV, and MenACWY do not meaningfully prevent transmission, as detailed in the following link with supporting citations: https://t.co/GDMW14ps3R.  Also see an FDA Briefing Document, dated September 20, 2024, titled Use of Controlled Human Infection Models to Support Licensure of Pertussis Vaccines which explains that “aP [acellular pertussis] containing vaccines induce helper T cells (TH2) memory and neutralizing antibody responses that effectively prevent symptomatic disease but fail to prevent colonization and carriage.”[7]

In a similar vein, HPV is almost exclusively transmitted through sexual contact, and, in most cases, an 11-year-old is not sexually active and may not face any meaningful near-term exposure risk. The decision to vaccinate at age 11 versus later should therefore be based on individualized considerations—anticipated timing of exposure, medical history, and parental values—rather than a uniform community-wide transmission concern. Hence, even putting the significant risks of this product aside, HPV vaccines should be recommended pursuant to SCDM so that clinicians and parents can evaluate risks, benefits, and timing for the individualized child, rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach.

As a final example, studies reflect that influenza vaccine has not been shown to meaningfully prevent transmission among children[8] and influenza vaccination during pregnancy involves widely varying clinical circumstances and risk profiles, and patients differ in their medical history, prior vaccine reactions, trimester-specific considerations, and personal values. A meaningful recommendation therefore requires an individualized discussion of expected risks and benefits, available alternatives, and the patient’s preferences—not a reflexive “routine” assumption. This approach is consistent with an evidence-based framework that prioritizes informed consent and individualized care, especially where community transmission benefits are not the driving rationale for giving this vaccine during pregnancy.

The bottom line is that every vaccine should forthwith be moved to the SCDM category so that they will be administered through counseling based on the individual’s circumstances. HHS should eliminate all categories except for SCDM and treat all vaccines like every other drug or medical procedure.

Sources:

text:
Experiences with Maha Periyava: Nandhanar Parampara

He belonged to the Nandanar hierarchy!

Once Sri Maha Periyava was returning to SriMatham camp in Brahmins street after visiting a temple of village deity. With Him were about seven or eight persons, mostly His devotees and helpers.

On the way, there was a small causeway with two feet-high walls on either side. (Culvert). On one of those were placed a lot of vegetables such as pumpkins (both the red and white variety), coconut, broad beans (avaraikkaay), tender coconut and groundnuts. Every one was surprised to see them now, since they were not there when they went towards the temple. But a more and bigger surprise awaited them.

Sri Maha Periyava stopped near the culvert wall. About fifteen feet away, a man (belonging to the ‘backward community’ Balu Mama used to call him ‘Thirukkulath thiruththondan’ [திருக்குலத் திருத்தொண்டன்]) with folded hands, and expression full of devotion was standing with all humility.

Tears were about to roll down his cheeks.

Periyava instead of standing in one place, started to turn around one way and the other (sort of self-pradhakshinam) many times, and was talking to the devotees without any pretext! Yes, some childish blabbers with no connection to that situation!

What was the necessity for that talk? No one understood!

Then He told the devotees to ask that man why he had kept those items there.

“I have kept them for ‘Saami’ only (he was referring to Periyava as ‘Saami’). All these were grown in the garden. I saw ‘Saami’ going to the temple. Knowing that He will return this way only, I ran back and brought these from my house. ‘Saami’ will not accept if I offer milk or curd. But, will accept these, will he not?” said he.

Periyava indicated to His helper to take all of them.

“Like Sri Rama accepted what was offered by Guhan (the boatman).He (Rama) was an example, who showed the way! All these vegetables are the offerings to Lord Chandramouleeswarar tomorrow!’

After about ten steps, He turned around and looked at him for a second. The man was wiping off tears from his eyes!

Periyava didn’t speak for the next five minutes.

“Tell me, those who prostrate before me, will they be able to see my back?”

“No, they can’t”

“What should be done if they want to see the back?”

“They should do ‘pradhakshinam’ of Periyava”

There was a heavy silence for one minute!

“Otherwise, I should do self-pradakshinam in front of him… then he can see all sides, isn’t it?”

Everybody was awestruck!

‘Oh! That’s it! All His drama near the culvert was for this, Atma--pradhakshinam! Is it so?’

‘For whom? For which ‘Shiva bhaktha’, did He give him His darshan?’

Yes, for him; that true devotee’

For the devotees, the vegetables were like the fruits Sabari offered to Sri Rama! The white pumpkin was like a ‘Shivalinga’, the ash on it was like the sacred ash!

They reached the camp.

“He belongs to the Nandhanar hierarchy…” saying this, Periyava entered inside.

(Those who were witness to this incident, felt very emotional. Because even heads of States were not known to have had that type of darshan. In Periyava’s vision, that man was a true ‘Parameshwara Bhaktha’. Is any other qualification that was required?)

Narrated by SriMatham Balu Mama
Source: Mahaperiaval Darisana Anubhavangal Vol. 6
Compiled by Jagadguru Sri Maha Periyava - Kanchi Paramacharya/Fb

text:
Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, and he was greatly perplexed because some were saying, “John has been raised from the dead”; others were saying, “Elijah has appeared”; still others, “One of the ancient prophets has arisen.” But Herod said, “John I beheaded. Who then is this about whom I hear such things?” And he kept trying to see him. Luke 9:7–9

Something peculiar happens when those who refuse to live according to God’s will witness His presence in the lives of others—they become unsettled, even confused. Herod was one of these souls. Though Jewish by name, he lived a life of self-indulgence, pride, and moral compromise. Upon hearing of Jesus and His mighty works, Herod’s fascination was mingled with inner disturbance. His conscience was especially agitated by guilt over his execution of John the Baptist.

Herod’s perplexity did not arise from a sincere openness to faith, but from fear, guilt, and superstition. Sin had so darkened his heart that he could not perceive the grace of God manifest in Christ. The Gospel tells us that despite Herod’s interior turmoil, “he kept trying to see Him.” This desire reveals a divided soul—one curious about the truth, yet unwilling to embrace it.

Herod offers us not an example of virtue, but a warning. Those who resist the will of God may still catch glimpses of Him through the holiness of others. But without repentance, such encounters bring neither peace nor clarity. In Herod’s case, his fascination resulted first in torment, then in silence. When Jesus finally stood before Herod during the Passion, our Lord did not utter a word. That silence was a judgment upon his hardened heart.

Looking at Herod’s life, many might have envied him. He was rich, powerful, dined in luxury, lived in magnificent palaces, and enjoyed the protection of Rome. Though such monarchs are rare today, the allure of worldly wealth and fame remains strong. The modern equivalents—the celebrities, influencers, and elite—draw millions of admirers. Social media exalts their lifestyles, while the world glorifies indulgence, comfort, and social prestige.

But to what end? Is it to enjoy life in the moment, seizing every earthly pleasure? What happens when this life ends and we stand before the Judgment Seat of God? At that hour, every fleeting comfort will vanish, and we will be left with the state of our soul. Herod’s worldly success was ultimately empty. He lacked peace in this life, and, without conversion, his eternal fate was sealed in that same unrest.

Herod’s life is depicted in the Gospels for a reason. From his example, we must lift the veil of worldly and sensory indulgence and see them for what they are—not only in light of their eternal consequences, but also the interior ruin they cause even now. Such a life has no power to save, no ability to satisfy beyond the moment, and always leaves the soul perplexed and curious—a curiosity that ends in confusion.

Those whose hearts are fixed on such indulgence will always hunger for more and never be satisfied. The best way to avoid the lure of sinful indulgence is to immerse ourselves in the purifying truths of the Gospel. Truth both purifies and liberates. It frees the soul to become the temple of God it was created to be—radiant with holiness, living in joyful union with Him and in spiritual communion with others. Nothing could be greater in this life, and nothing else will satisfy in the next.

Reflect today on any lingering confusion, fear, or disordered curiosity you may carry when encountering Christ in your life. Do you approach Him like Herod—curious but uncommitted—or with a heart that is ready to be purified and transformed? Let the example of Herod lead you away from perplexity and into conversion. Truth Himself stands before you. Do not remain merely curious. Surrender in faith, and the riches of God’s Kingdom will be yours.

Lord of true riches, the power, wealth, and fleshly indulgences of this world are seductive.

Did you know Nebraska incentivizes petroleum too? Meanwhile, E15 pays the same Nebraska motor-fuel tax as gasoline. The 8¢ E15 credit is a capped incentive designed to encourage retailers to offer a higher-ethanol fuel, not an exemption from the fuel tax, and the cap stopped payments in August. 

And the “33% less energy” claim needs context. That compares 100% ethanol with 100% gasoline, not E15 with regular E10. Since regular gasoline already contains about 10% ethanol, moving from E10 to E15 reduces energy content by only about 1.7% per gallon, not 33%. So if we’re comparing the fuels consumers actually see at the pump, 33% is a pretty misleading number to use. And look at the pic, it is a ~18% discount, saving you money.

text: The reason the 3-finger test works right now is specifically that current video deepfake models render hands badly, real-time face-swap and voice-clone tech has gotten very convincing but hand articulation under occlusion and odd angles is still a weak point in most live-generation pipelines, so it's a genuinely useful heuristic today. The problem is treating it as a durable defense rather than a snapshot of a temporary model limitation, hand rendering is a known, actively-being-solved problem in generative video, and any test that relies on "the AI is bad at X" has a shelf life measured in product cycles, not years. The more durable version of this defense isn't a physical gesture test at all, it's structural: legitimate technical interviews from actual companies follow predictable patterns (scheduled through official calendaring systems, conducted on standard platforms with verifiable company domains, and critically, never require running unreviewed code from a private repo as a "coding test" before an offer). The GitHub repo push is the actual attack, the deepfake video call is just the delivery mechanism to build enough trust that the target runs the code without scrutinizing it, and that same social-engineering goal could be achieved with a text-only recruiter conversation just as easily if the developer's guard is already down from thinking a "real" video interview validated the opportunity. Test the code in an isolated VM or container regardless of who's asking, that assumption holds even after deepfake detection stops working.

text:
Quit watching Fox News dummy. They are afraid of Gavin Newsome. 

You've got the causation exactly backwards, so let's fix that first and then get to who actually approved these taxes.

California isn't expensive because it needs money. 

It's expensive because 39 million people and half the world's tech industry want to live in the same 100 miles of coastline and bid the housing up. 

The gap between California and Texas in taxes is a few percentage points of income. 

You said: "They can't fund themselves" 

California sends about $650 billion a year to Washington and gets less back per person than it pays. 

It funds itself and Mississippi. The states that literally can't fund themselves without money from somewhere else are the ones getting $1.50 to $2.00 back per dollar. 

You've described the donor as the dependent.

Now the part you'll like least: Californians keep voting for these taxes. 

On purpose. By name.

Prop 30 (2012) — the 13.3% top income tax rate on millionaires. Voters passed it 55–45. Prop 55 (2016) extended it to 2030 — passed 63–37. Marin, San Francisco, and Santa Clara — where the millionaires actually live — voted yes.

Prop 63 (2004) — the 1% millionaire's tax for mental health. Voter-approved.

Prop 56 (2016) — $2-a-pack tobacco tax. 64% yes.
Prop 6 (2018) — a ballot measure to repeal the gas tax increase. Voters rejected the repeal 57–43. They were offered lower gas taxes and said no thanks.

Measure M (2016) — LA County's half-cent transit sales tax. 71% yes. Measure H (2017), the homelessness sales tax — 69% yes.

Props 1 and 2 (2024) — $6.4 billion mental health bond and $10 billion school bond. Both passed.

And it cuts the other way, which is the point: California voters can reject taxes and do. 

Prop 13 (1978) capped property taxes at 1% and required a two-thirds legislative vote for any state tax increase — the strictest anti-tax rule in the country, still in force. 

Prop 30 (2022), a new tax on income over $2 million, went down 58–42. 

Every local sales tax, parcel tax, and school bond in California has to go on a ballot. 

This is the hardest state in the country to raise a tax in without asking the people paying it — which means every tax you're calling "extreme" is one that survived a public vote.

True democracy. 

So the picture isn't a state "held up" by taxes it extracts from unwilling citizens. 

It's the fourth-largest economy on Earth whose residents periodically walk into a booth and vote to tax themselves to pay for transit, schools, and mental health, and periodically vote not to when they think it's too much. 

That's not a failed state. That's the thing the founders called self-government, working roughly as designed, in a place rich enough to afford it.

Maybe broke ass Red Sates could learn alot from th 4th largest economy in the world.

text:
Plenty of people have expressed their opinions on this, but what do actual college decision-makers think? Here are 3 quotes from current general managers in college football. 

P4 GM: "Exposure has never been easier.  College summer camps, summer combines/camps, increased unofficial visits, larger game day visits, easy access to putting your film online (HUDL).  Most kids that aren’t being recruited by the schools they want to be isn’t a visibility issue; it’s a talent issue.  High School families don’t need to be paying to get evaluated.  They should start with their HS coaches and find out how to become a better football player." 

P4 GM: "They’re just trying to make money on the dreams of the players who wouldn’t get recruited anyway. Are there now more spots for FBS teams to take players? No. They’ll just rank more players who paid for it, but the opportunities don’t expand. The number of scholarships given out by programs remains the same. Excited for the meltdown because On3 is a market driver for NIL and this opens the door for families to pay them to rank them higher for more NIL." 

G5 GM: "To me, it's all stupid. Anybody who's paying for these rankings or evaluations is already in the wrong. The priority should just be to be a really good high school football player, and you're going to be recruited, and you're going to get ranked. 

"Are these parents even going to listen when they get a rating back that says they're an FCS-level player? Probably not. They'll probably just spend more money trying to change what they are. They'll keep spending money on things until they get the answer they want to hear, but the film isn't going to change from Friday nights."
